unlocks.conditions: Hold a UK visa or UK residence permit valid on the day of entry into Georgia and present a travel and/or other appropriate document proving its validity. Visa-free stays are limited to 90 calendar days in any 180-day period; this UK-document exemption does not require a multiple-entry visa.

source.verificationPath: Legislative Herald of Georgia > Ordinance No 256 of 5 June 2015 > annex item 12 (United Kingdom) and Notes 1–2; read alongside the 17 April 2025 amendment No 122
source.exactQuote: Aliens holding a visa and/or a residence permit of any country listed in the annex may enter and stay in Georgia without visa for 90 calendar days in any 180-day period.
source.validityQuote: For the purpose of entering and staying in Georgia without visa, a visa and/or a residence permit of a respective country shall be valid on the day of entry into Georgia (crossing the border), which must be evidenced by a travel and/or other appropriate document.
source.notes: The English page explicitly identifies itself as the initial edition. The current change list contains the 17 April 2025 amendment No 122; its Georgian text adds the special multiple-entry/one-year conditions for specified Gulf-state documents, not UK documents. The amendment was read directly, rather than treating the initial English edition as the final consolidated text.

unlocks.notes: The 90-day allowance is cumulative within any 180-day period, not a new 90 days per entry. The visa/residence document must be valid at the Georgian border and evidenced by an appropriate document. This corrects the existing UK entry’s unsupported multiple-entry restriction; other Georgian admission requirements still apply and no right to work, study or reside is established.

source.exactQuote: Artículo 2. Al momento de ingresar a territorio panameño, los ciudadanos extranjeros deberán mantener una visa vigente otorgada por uno de los países mencionados en el artículo primero del Decreto Ejecutivo No. 521 de 6 de agosto de 2018.
source.qualifyingCountriesVerificationPath: Executive Decree No. 521 of 6 August 2018 > page 1, Article 1 lists Canada, the United States, Australia, Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom, Singapore and EU member states
source.notes: Article 1 of Decree No. 196 replaces the full prior Article 2. The superseded Article 2 required a multiple-entry visa, previous use in the issuing state, and at least six months remaining validity; the replacement requires only a qualifying visa valid upon entry.

unlocks.notes: This entry covers the qualifying visa exemption for tourism, not a right to work or reside in Panama. unlocks.conditions: Only ordinary-passport nationals of India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam may use a qualifying UK visa or residence document to apply for a Taiwan Travel Authorization Certificate (TAC). A valid UK entry visa (including electronic visa), resident/permanent resident certificate, or one expired less than 10 years before arrival may qualify, subject to all NIA conditions.

source.pageSection: English instructions > Basic requirements; Special requirements 1; Notes 1-3, 5-8 and 10; landing-page Cambodia notice
source.verificationPath: NIA TAC portal > select English > Next > Next > read Basic requirements, Special requirements and Notes (before the personal application form)
source.exactQuote: The holder of an TAC may stay in Taiwan for 14 days, starting from the next day of arrival.
source.nationalityQuote: Nationals of India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, and Vietnam can apply online for an R.O.C.(Taiwan) Travel Authorization Certificate (TAC)
source.documentQuote: The applicant possesses at least one of the following documents issued by the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, any of EU and Schengen countries, New Zealand, Australia, Japan
source.validityQuote: An approved TAC is valid for 90 days. Multiple entries within these 90 days are allowed.

unlocks.notes: TAC is a conditional travel authorization, not a Taiwan eVisa or a general exemption for every UK-visa holder. Approval is valid 90 days with multiple entries, but each stay is 14 days starting the day after arrival, and TAC entries are limited to six per calendar year. Expired-document eligibility is strictly less than 10 years before arrival; if no expiry/validity period is shown, NIA measures from issue date. Cambodia is not eligible for new TAC applications from 1 August 2026; previously approved TACs have the stated transitional exception. Other NIA routes and visa rules are outside this entry.
unlocks.additionalRequirements: Apply online and obtain approval before travel; print the TAC and present it with the qualifying UK document at entry. Ordinary passport must remain valid at least six months from arrival, and an onward/return air or ferry ticket is required. Applicant must never have been employed as a migrant worker in Taiwan and must have no record of immigration irregularities or legal violations in Taiwan. Work permits alone and visas stamped VOID, CANCELLED or CANCELLED WITHOUT PREJUDICE do not qualify.

unlocks.conditions: The Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme is limited to eligible passport holders from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bahrain, China, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kuwait, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Oman, Peru, the Philippines, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Thailand, Türkiye, Uzbekistan or Vietnam. Hold a qualifying UK short-stay visit visa and first land and gain lawful entry to the UK using the current visa. Prior lawful UK entry is required for each distinct period of UK permission. The entire Irish visit must end before the current UK permission expires. A UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) alone does not qualify.
unlocks.additionalRequirements: For nationals of Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Peru, the page's special note requires an existing valid short-stay UK visa issued before 1 February 2024, including a multi-entry UK visa; a UK ETA is insufficient. UK transit and marriage/civil-partnership visitor visas do not qualify. Long-stay UK permissions and BRP cards alone do not qualify. Direct travel from outside the UK is possible only after prior lawful UK entry under the current permission and within its remaining validity.

source.pageSection: Who is eligible; Eligible Countries and notes 1-3; UK short stay visas; How to use the visa waiver programme; How long can I stay in Ireland?
source.verificationPath: Observed page breadcrumb: Home > Coming to visit Ireland > Short stay visa waiver programme. Read the eligibility table, its notes, permitted UK visa types, prior UK entry and maximum-stay sections.
source.exactQuote: The Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme allows nationals of certain countries, who have entered the UK on foot of certain UK short stay visas, to travel to Ireland without the requirement to obtain an Irish visa.
source.stayQuote: The maximum amount of time you can come to Ireland for under the programme is for 90 days, or the remaining time left on you UK permission, whichever is the least amount of time.
source.etaQuote: Please note that an ETA cannot be used to avail of the SSVWP, any National in possession of an ETA and not a UK Visa will need a separate Irish visa if they wish to travel to the State.
source.notes: Current government page retrieved with HTTP 200 on the access date; its own last-updated assertion is 9 May 2025. The canonical link uses /coming-to-visit-ireland/short-stay-visa-waiver-programme/.

unlocks.notes: 90 days is only the maximum ceiling: permitted stay is the lesser of 90 days and remaining UK permission, subject to admission. This is the Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, not the separate British-Irish Visa Scheme. Ghana and other passport countries absent from the eligibility list are not covered. Ukrainian nationals, and holders of Hong Kong or Macau passports, are noted by the source as already Irish-visa-exempt independently and are not counted here as gaining an additional entitlement from a UK visa. No work, study or residence permission is established by this visitor exemption.
